items.title: Canada Demand for Tariff Relief on Trucks Imperiled Trade Talks
items.author: Josh Wingrove
items.content: <article>Trade talks between the US and Canada collapsed Friday in part amid a last-minute standoff over cutting US tariffs on Canadian medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, people familiar with the matter said.</article>

items.title: Smithsonian Plan for Latino Museum Would Avoid Vote in Congress
items.author: Robin Pogrebin
items.content: <article>The board will vote whether to house the museum in its Arts and Industries Building rather than build on a site owned by the National Park Service.</article>

items.title: Canada Sets US Counter-Tariffs Sept. 8 to Mirror Trump Levy
items.author: Thomas Seal and Derek Decloet
items.content: <article>Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada will apply dollar-for-dollar counter-tariffs on US imports on Sept. 8, escalating the feud rocking one of the world’s biggest trading relationships.</article>

items.title: Russia Considers Grain Purchases to Offset Export Disruptions
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Russia’s government is planning a series of measures to support grain producers, include crop procurement, preferential loan extensions and sales subsidies, Interfax reported, citing Agriculture Minister Oksana Lut.</article>

items.title: Some States Banned the Use of Food Stamps to Buy Soda. Did It Work?
items.author: Ben Blatt
items.content: <article>A study shows a modest decline in soda purchases, but it’s not clear that the results will hold up in the long run.</article>

items.title: Trump’s Economic Isolation Plan Risks Iran Strikes Across Gulf
items.author: Eric Martin
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump is betting new sanctions, a naval blockade and ramped-up economic pressure against Iran’s trading partners can accomplish what thousands of bombs and missiles could not: force Tehran to accept a deal to end the war on US terms.</article>

items.title: Trade Breakdown Deepens US Canada Rift
items.content: <article>US-Canada trade talks collapsed late Friday, triggering 50% US tariffs on about $20 billion of Canadian goods and a pledge from Prime Minister Mark Carney to retaliate dollar for dollar. Joining Bloomberg This Weekend are Bloomberg White House Correspondent Jeff Mason and Bloomberg Markets and Economic Columnist Jonathan Levin to discuss how the dispute could deepen a lasting rupture between the allies while tariff-driven inflation, rising Treasury yields and the $40 trillion US debt load complicate the administration’s economic message ahead of the midterms. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Sweden’s Kristersson Cancels Campaign Speech After School Attack
items.author: Charlie Duxbury
items.content: <article>Sweden’s Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson canceled a campaign speech for next month’s general election after a sword attack at a school left a 17-year-old girl dead and three others injured.</article>

items.title: US Envoy Warns Israel on Syria Base Attack Near Turkish Border
items.author: Taylan Bilgic
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump’s envoy for Syria and Iraq issued a stern warning after Israel’s recent strike on a long-shuttered military base near the Turkish border, invoking the downing of a Russian jet more than a decade ago that escalated regional tensions.</article>

items.title: Manchester City Financial Rules Verdict Hangs Over UK’s Relations With Emiratis
items.author: Alex Dooler and Giles Turner
items.content: Prime Minister Andy Burnham faces an awkward moment when a commission finally rules on the Premier League club’s legal saga.

items.title: Putin Acknowledges Economic Impact From Ukraine’s Refinery Hits
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Vladimir Putin lauded the “heroes” of his military in stepping up a campaign on Ukrainian targets, calling the strikes effective and timely while acknowledging that reciprocal attacks by Ukraine have caused economic damage.</article>

items.title: Switzerland’s Big Food Question Keeps Voters Busy at Ballot Box
items.author: Fabrice Obrist
items.content: <article>Switzerland will soon go to the polls on the issue of food, in yet another test of voters’ appetites to answer big questions at the ballot box.</article>

items.title: Reform UK Feuds Sidetrack Nigel Farage’s Push to Prepare Party to Lead
items.author: Lucy White
items.content: <article>Reform UK is struggling to professionalize its insurgency against the British political establishment, with infighting over its direction spilling into the open just as Nigel Farage’s party seeks to convince voters it’s an enduring electoral force.</article>

items.title: US Hits Canada With 50% Tariffs as Carney Vows to Retaliate
items.author: Josh Wingrove, Alicia Diaz and Thomas Seal
items.content: <article>US-Canada trade talks fell apart just before a midnight deadline, with 50% tariffs hitting billions of dollars of Canadian goods and Prime Minister Mark Carney vowing to retaliate in a dispute that looks poised to intensify.</article>

items.title: We Tried to Cover a Tom Kean Campaign Event. Someone Called the Police.
items.author: Tracey Tully
items.content: <article>Representative Thomas Kean Jr. was joined Friday on the campaign trail by House Speaker Mike Johnson. An aide to Mr. Kean blocked a reporter’s entry. Then the police were called.</article>

items.title: Pentagon Fires Editor and Publisher of Independent Military Publication
items.author: Minho Kim
items.content: <article>The firings at Stars and Stripes also claimed a Middle East correspondent. They are the latest effort by the Pentagon to diminish the news outlet’s editorial independence.</article>

items.title: Drawing on His Rust Belt Roots, Vance Campaigns for Republicans
items.author: Zolan Kanno-Youngs
items.content: <article>Vice President JD Vance traveled to his hometown, Middletown, Ohio, and spoke at a steel factory where his grandfather once worked.</article>

items.title: U.S. Agreed to Pay Liberia $5 Million in Connection with Deportees, Documents Say
items.author: Madeleine Ngo, Hamed Aleaziz and Zolan Kanno-Youngs
items.content: <article>The Trump administration approved the payment after Liberia said it would consider taking migrants from other countries.</article>

items.title: Trump Accounts Get an Unlikely Endorser: Gavin Newsom
items.author: Laurel Rosenhall
items.content: <article>Mr. Newsom, the governor of California, normally has harsh words for President Trump. But he called the new children’s savings accounts “one of the best things” the president has done.</article>

items.title: Trump’s New Midterm Pitch to Voters: Pretend I’m on Ballot
items.author: Hadriana Lowenkron and Catherine Lucey
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump tried out a new campaign message on Friday, telling voters in South Carolina to “pretend” he was on the ballot and turn out to back his hand-picked candidate, Senator Darline Graham, in a contentious Republican primary.</article>

items.title: 5 Deportees Are Flown by US to Equatorial Guinea After they Resist Deplaning in Liberia
items.author: Pranav Baskar, Hamed Aleaziz and Genevieve Glatsky
items.content: <article>At least five of the people flown to Liberia under the Trump administration’s third-country deportation program resisted leaving the plane. They were then flown to Equatorial Guinea.</article>

items.title: Canada Nears Trump Trade Deal | Balance of Power 8/21/2026
items.content: <article>"Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Canada's former Minister of International Trade Mary Ng, former National Security Advisor to President Trump John Bolton, CSIS Senior Nonresident Scholar Clayton Seigle, Rebelle Communications Founder & CEO Laura Fink, and Stonecourt Capital LP Rick Davis. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Anwar’s One-Time Ally Turns Rival With New Malaysia Party
items.author: Netty Ismail and Ram Anand
items.content: <article>When Rafizi Ramli married in 2011, Malaysia’s future prime minister, Anwar Ibrahim, hosted a celebration at his home. Fifteen years later, the former allies are now political rivals, with Rafizi setting the groundwork to one day sideline his former benefactor.</article>

items.title: Leavitt Says She’ll Return to MAGA Inc. After White House
items.author: Hadriana Lowenkron
items.content: <article>White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said she will return to MAGA Inc., the president’s super political action committee, when she leaves her post later this month.</article>

items.title: Seigle: Squeezing Iran Means Confronting China
items.content: <article>Senior Nonresident Scholar at the Center for Strategic and International Studies Clayton Seigle says a successful US economic pressure campaign against Iran would require confronting China, a major buyer of Iranian energy, potentially putting Washington's "fragile trade war détente" with Beijing at risk. Seigle says tougher pressure could also push energy prices higher if Iran retaliates against shipping or regional infrastructure, with US gasoline prices an important political concern ahead of the midterms. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's 'Balance of Power.' (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: 'Hopeful' US. Canada Will Reach Deal: Fmr. Trade Official
items.content: <article>Former Canadian Trade Minister Mary Ng says she is hopeful the US and Canada can reach a trade agreement before Friday's deadline, pointing to positive signals from negotiators on both sides. Ng also says Canada should continue diversifying its trade relationships, pointing to opportunities across Asia including Japan, South Korea, Singapore and Indonesia. She speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's 'Balance of Power.' (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Court Slashes Award Alex Jones Was Ordered to Pay Sandy Hook Parents
items.author: Elizabeth Williamson
items.content: <article>An appeals court reduced the award to the parents of one victim to $6 million from $49 million, citing a Texas damages cap. The conspiracy theorist owes over $1 billion in other cases.</article>

items.title: US and Canada Race Against Clock to Hammer Out Trade Deal
items.author: Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Josh Wingrove and Joe Deaux
items.content: <article>US and Canadian negotiators haggled Friday over terms of a trade deal that would cut tariffs and retaliatory measures between the two major trading partners, with signs of optimism that a pact would be finalized before a midnight deadline in Washington.</article>

items.title: Prison Firm Donated to Trump’s PAC After ICE Gave It $165 Million a Year in Contracts
items.author: Kenneth P. Vogel and Hamed Aleaziz
items.content: <article>The GEO Group has profited from the administration’s mass deportation campaign. A subsidiary donated more than $1.4 million to the president’s super PAC last month.</article>

items.title: America Ends a Summer of Lightning-Fast Primaries and Political Speed Dating
items.author: Jess Bidgood
items.content: <article>Plot twists in several states have led to rapid-fire races that have felt more reminiscent of European-style snap campaigns than traditional American marathons.</article>

items.title: Chief Justice Allows Trump to Continue White House Ballroom Construction, for Now
items.author: Ann E. Marimow
items.content: <article>The 90,000-square-foot ballroom project has grown in size and scope, with the president’s lawyers saying it is intertwined with the renovation of an underground military bunker.</article>

items.title: Lula Calls Trump to Resume Talks Over US Tariffs on Brazil
items.author: Simone Iglesias
items.content: <article>President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva urged Donald Trump to resume negotiations over US tariffs on Brazil during a Friday phone call, seeking to soothe relations with Washington ahead of the country’s October election.</article>

items.title: Gazebos From Uzbekistan: The Latest Foreign Gifts in Trump’s Washington
items.author: Luke Broadwater
items.content: <article>The structures will go up in West Potomac Park, the site of President Trump’s planned National Garden of American Heroes.</article>
